extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and practicing investigative journalists, journalism students, and newsroom editors
extracted.subtask_description: Practical rubric and methodological guidance for pursuing investigative news stories, codified from Bob Woodward's Watergate-era lessons. Covers high-level principles, implicit newsworthiness criteria, and specific investigative methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Patient
rubrics_metrics.description: "It often takes weeks, months, or years" — stories develop in stages; Watergate took 26 months from break-in to Nixon resignation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not publish prematurely; persistence over scoops. Treat investigations as long-term projects that may require waiting for corroboration, documents, or evolving patterns before reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build Trust with Sources
rubrics_metrics.description: "People agree to be sources because they want their side to be heard" — make lists of everyone connected to the case and approach sources thoughtfully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach sources at home or off-hours, listen rather than just interrogate, protect anonymity when promised, and cultivate relationships over years. Consider comprehensive mapping of all potential source contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify Everything
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm with at least one other source; prefer documents over human sources where possible; re-interview repeatedly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek documentary corroboration (paper trail) where available; require secondary confirmation even for high-profile sources (example: Deep Throat was confirmed via another source). Continuously question your own assumptions and re-test theories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence from Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: "All good work is done in defiance of management" — prioritize reporters' instincts over corporate caution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue stories the establishment would prefer buried; hold power accountable regardless of position. Be prepared to push against management or institutional pressure to ensure accountability reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hidden truth (newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: A story should reveal a hidden truth that powerful actors want concealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations should aim at uncovering concealed wrongdoing or information suppressed by those in power; presence of deliberate concealment increases newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple sources willing to corroborate (newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be multiple sources who can corroborate the central claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for independent confirmers rather than relying on one account; corroboration across sources strengthens publishability and reduces risk of error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document trail (newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: A document trail that can be independently verified is a key criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek paper records — financial, legal, governmental — that substantiate claims; documents are prioritized over sole reliance on human testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public interest of fundamental constitutional weight (newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: The story should have clear public interest, ideally of fundamental constitutional importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize investigations with implications for public rights, governance, corruption, or other constitutional concerns that affect the broader public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patience-tolerant story (newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: The story must be tolerant of delays — it won't expire if delayed for verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the story will remain relevant after extended development; avoid leads that will vanish or be irretrievable if not immediately publishable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scalable — initial tip leads to broader pattern (newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: An initial tip should plausibly lead to a broader pattern or systemic issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a lead can be expanded from isolated incidents to revealing institutional patterns or wider significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verifiable through paper records (newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: The story should be verifiable through paper records such as financial, legal, or governmental documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize leads that can be checked against durable records rather than ephemeral testimony alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance — affects nation, not just niche (newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer investigations that affect the nation or have broad significance, rather than narrow niche impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gauge the scope and magnitude of harm or public importance when deciding to pursue resource-intensive investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reform potential — exposure could change something (newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that have the potential to prompt reform or meaningful change are especially worthy of investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether publication is likely to lead to accountability, policy change, legal action, or institutional reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the money (method)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Follow the money" — trace financial flows to reveal motives and connections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use financial records, transaction histories, and accounting documents to establish links between actors and actions; money trails can provide objective evidence of wrongdoing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reverse-pyramid investigation (method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reverse-pyramid investigation: start from suspicion and work to proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with a hypothesis or suspicion and then systematically gather corroborating evidence (sources, documents) until the story supports definitive reporting; do not begin by assuming the conclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Door-to-door interviewing of low-level staffers (method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct door-to-door interviews of low-level staffers to uncover overlooked information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage with peripheral or lower-ranking people connected to an institution — they may provide candid details and leads that higher-ups conceal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use deep-background sources to test theories (method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use deep-background sources to test and refine investigative theories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ anonymous or off-the-record experts to challenge, corroborate, or refine working hypotheses; treat deep-background information as a tool to shape reporting while still seeking on-the-record confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-reference financial records with political activities (method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-referencing financial records with political activities to establish connections and timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match transactions, donations, or financial movements with timelines of political decisions or events to show correlation or causation; use cross-referencing to strengthen narrative and evidentiary links.
